Dear Dr. O'Brien,

Re: Ms Janet Bird

Thank you for seeing Ms Janet, a 16-year-old student whose features are suggestive of anorexia nervosa.       Commented [ESL1]: Ms Bird
                                                                                                              (And on subsequent occasions.)
On 11/11/2007, she presented with a 3 month history of constipation. Her bowel action was once every 4        Commented [ESL2]: 3-month
to 5 days despite taking two tablespoons bran in the morning. Her examination was unremarkable apart          Commented [ESL3]: of
from low weight which was 52 kg. She requested a strong laxative. However, I refused and advised her to
increase vegetables, fluids and fibre in her diet.

Ms Janet's mother accompanied her on 28/12/2007 and she was warried regarding Janet's weight. On              Commented [ESL4]: spelling
examination, she lost 5 kg of her weight in a month. Otherwise, no abnormalities were detected.               Commented [ESL5]: had
Accordingly, thyroid function tests, liver function tests and full blood exam were requested.                 Commented [ESL6]: a

On today's visit, I discovered that she had had false believe about her weight. She wanted her weight to be   Commented [ESL7]: beliefs
40 kg. Moreover, she complained of over-reacting parents. Please note, her laboratory results were normal
and she denied vomiting.

In view of the above, I would appreciate it if you provide an assessment of this patient as well as advice    Commented [ESL8]: would
regarding management and treatment of her condition.

Should you have any queries, please do not hesitate to contact me.

Yours sincerely,

Doctor
